claim: Few computers can run great local models; few have dedicated GPUs or 32 GB+ VRAM
evidence: Steam Jul 2026: 51.4% have 10 GB+; 5.4% have 24 GB; 32 GB bucket not retrieved; gamer sample.

claim: A 24 GB Mac uses ~10 GB with a few windows open
evidence: Measured 9.67 GB after startup, 12.92 GB with apps open.

claim: Even 32 GB VRAM may not suffice with other apps open
evidence: Extrapolation; no 32 GB test.

claim: DGX Spark started at ~$4,000, now $6-7k
evidence: $3,999 to $4,699 (Feb) to $6,950 (Oct, 128 GB); 64 GB at $4,999; partner systems $7-9k.

claim: High-end Apple computers cost like a small car did ten years ago
evidence: Comparison not sourced. Top configurations cost several thousand dollars; no primary-source figure verified. Recommend dropping the comparison.

claim: 2-3% of US households pay for AI (credit card analysis)
evidence: BofA ~3%, PNC 2.2%. Banks and card panels, not 'credit card companies'. a16z: 4.5% of consumers.

claim: 97% of users use AI for free
evidence: Replaced by US card-data range: 2.2-4.5% of households or consumers pay. Menlo 2025 (~3%) is an implied revenue ratio; Menlo 2026 reports 55% of AI users pay (survey, different denominator, not used in the report body).

claim: Local AI is 'cheaper' but most people already use AI for free
evidence: Cost argument matters mainly to paying minority; top 1% = 19.5% of spend.

claim: Privacy is a weak argument; users accept Meta/Google trade-offs
evidence: Surveys show high stated concern, high disclosure, low awareness.

claim: Half the apps are underwhelming; the other half deliver but below frontier
evidence: Result of the author's own tests (linked in 4.2): 4 of 8 scored apps at 2 or below; n=9.

claim: More than 75% of apps show no download time estimate
evidence: 60% of 5 evaluated apps (3 of 5); 3 of 8 at minimum.

claim: No app tells the user the model's cut-off date
evidence: Not recorded in tests.

claim: Apps list many models without size or purpose
evidence: True for Draw Things, DiffusionBee; not for BoBe, Msty.

claim: Local image apps cannot refine a single picture (cruise ship)
evidence: One app, one model; control misuse suspected; other edit tools untested.

claim: Image model could not render Heidelberg castle; ChatGPT (5) could a year ago
evidence: First half observed in the DiffusionBee test. Second half is the author's recollection (ChatGPT 5); the earlier output was not kept.

claim: Local models are 6-12 months behind frontier
evidence: ~4 months for largest open models; 6-12 for consumer-GPU size; practical lag likely longer.

claim: The 6-12 month claim assumes you have the right computer
evidence: Epoch limits it to models fitting 24-32 GB GPUs.

claim: Google Trends interest in local AI fell substantially since summer 2026
evidence: 'local ai' peak 100 (31 May 2026), 15 on 18 Oct 2026; 36% below Oct-Nov 2025 on four-week averages; abrupt step in the week of 12 Jul. Unexplained: other indicators (Ollama developers, Hugging Face downloads, author's other trends) rise while Trends falls. Worldwide index, 12 months.

claim: China is a big local-AI market; other countries minuscule
evidence: Model supply data only; no user data.

claim: Technology trends spread in waves from the US
evidence: Uneven diffusion from advanced economies is documented; the US is not first in AI usage (rank 21); local-AI pattern untested.

claim: AI hardware gets more expensive, unlike normal tech
evidence: Spark +74%; DRAM +49% QoQ; Dell/Lenovo +15-20%. Apple RAM upgrades unchanged in March.

claim: Hundreds of millions of capable devices by 2030
evidence: Gartner AI-PC shipments 220.8M (2025-26 forecast); NPU-based, not LLM-capable.

claim: Mobile will churn faster; Apple users will pay for on-device AI
evidence: Not measured.

claim: Hundreds of thousands of new apps within 1-2 years via vibe coding
evidence: No app-count series; HF downloads concentrated.

claim: About ten local-LLM apps in the iOS App Store
evidence: Apple DE search 'local AI': 10 results, 9 local-AI apps. A search page, not a store count.

claim: Most iOS apps are chatbot extensions
evidence: Not checked per app; 1 of 9 is an image generator. Directory: 74 of up to 315 listings are chat clients (all platforms).

claim: Little corporate or venture involvement
evidence: Runtime layer: funded (Ollama $65M, LM Studio ~$19M). Application layer: traces for 2 of 8 named apps, both small or old (GPT4All/Nomic $17M, 2023; AnythingLLM $0.5M note); none for 5. Author's inference: rounds are normally public, so few exist, early market. Author reports one contact app now has an investor (unverified, unnamed). No paid database queried.

claim: A local email-organising app would be a success
evidence: Product opinion.

claim: Local AI will grow faster than the AI market overall
evidence: Not tested.

claim: A local coding model could not read screenshots
evidence: True for Qwen3-Coder (text-only input); not for Qwen3-VL. Model used in the test to be confirmed.

claim: Very few local-AI apps have a good, fully developed user interface
evidence: In the author's 9 tests one app (LU) scored above 3 on onboarding (7 scored); four interface patterns recur. n=9, one tester, tester misreadings in at least 5 records; no data on typical users.

claim: Hardware and apps are likely to improve over the coming years if local AI follows the general technology path; AI coding tools speed up app development
evidence: Supported directionally: efficiency trend (to Apr 2025), memory capacity forecast from 2027-2028 (forecasts conflict), new app releases +60-104%. No projection of machines able to run a 30B model; app data not specific to local AI.
